capitals.name: Tranquebar (Fort Dansborg)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Fort Dansborg. Serampore was a second Danish seat (a Crown Regent from 1776). After the 1845 sale no seat is named; the Nicobars were administered from Tranquebar (Nicobar Islands page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Danish India row begins only in 1757. From the treaty of 20 November 1620 the Danes held Tranquebar and Fort Dansborg and nothing else of the mapped land; the factories at Masulipatnam (by 1625), Pipli (by 1625-26), Balasore (about 1636) and Calicut (1752-1791) were trading posts and are not drawn.

keyframe_review.note: 2,222 km2, 1757-1799: five cells, one at Serampore (West Bengal) and four in the Nicobars (bbox lon 88.3-93.9 E). Tranquebar, the Danes' oldest and principal settlement (capital, Fort Dansborg), is missing from the 1757-1799 shape (the polygon reaches west only to 88.3 E) and enters in 1800, and the West Bengal cell sits at 22.51 N 88.40 E, Calcutta's latitude, about 25 km south of Serampore (22.75 N 88.34 E), so it is displaced. The page gives no area, so the infobox cannot be compared. The British occupation of Serampore in 1763 is a ledger event, not a change of the shape.

keyframe_review.note: 322 km2, 1800-1802: bbox 79.8-88.5 E, 11.0-22.6 N, so the polygon holds Serampore and Tranquebar (the land grid registers only one West Bengal cell) but the Nicobars are gone, and Cliopatria shows nothing of the 1801-1802 British occupation of Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore. Danish sovereignty over all three continued; the occupation is drawn from the ledger.

region.text: the village of Tranquebar and the site of Fort Dansborg, granted by Raghunatha Nayak of Thanjavur

ledger.note: 20 November 1620: Denmark founds Tranquebar. The treaty with the Nayak of Tanjore (Raghunatha Nayak) 'was signed on 20 November 1620', granting the village and permission for a fort; a Danish treaty collection cited by the page dates it 19 November, and the Tharangambadi page says it 'was established on 19 November 1620 as the first Danish trading post in India'. Fort Dansborg was built from 1620. The page names the village, not its bounds, so the 15 km circle (the smallest that holds a land cell) is my reading.

region.text: Frederiksnagore (Serampore): Sripur, Akna and Serampore, acquired from the Nawab

ledger.note: October 1755: Frederiksnagore is established at Serampore. The Serampore page: the Danes obtained a parwana from Nawab Alivardi Khan and 'acquired three villages - Sripur, Akna, and Serampore - from the Nawab', paying 'an annual rent of 1601 sicca rupees to the local Zamindar'. The 6 km circle is my reading of three villages.

1 January 1756: the Nicobars are declared Danish property as Frederiksoerne. Colonisation failed by 1760 (malaria); the islands were administered from Tranquebar (Nicobar Islands page: colonisation began with the Danish East India Company 'in 1754/56') and the settlement was abandoned for good from 1848, while Danish sovereignty lasted to 1868.
1763: the British occupy Serampore. The page says only that they occupied it 'for the year', so the end is also 1763.
1763: the British leave Serampore after a year (the page gives no month).

1777: the colony passes from the Danish East India Company to the Crown. Infobox: 'Danish East India Company (1620-1777); Danish overseas colonies (1777-1869)'. Same state, same colour; Serampore's first Crown Regent, Colonel Ole Bie, took office in 1776 on the Serampore page.
1801: the British occupy Dansborg (Tranquebar), with Balasore and Frederiksnagore: 'British occupation 1801-1802'.
1801: the British occupy Frederiksnagore (Serampore); the page gives no day.
1802: the first British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends; the page gives the occupation as 1801-1802 and no day.
17 August 1802: a letter cited by the page reports the Danish flag hoisted again on Tranquebar's fort.
1808: the British occupy Frederiksnagore (Serampore) a second time (the page gives 1808-1815 for Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore, no month).

February 1808: Tranquebar is occupied again. 'Tranquebar was occupied by the British in February 1808 during the Napoleonic Wars but was restored to Denmark following the Treaty of Kiel in 1814.' Cliopatria's Danish India row ends in 1808 at this occupation.
1815: the second British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends (the page gives 1808-1815 and no day).

20 September 1815: Tranquebar is handed back. The Kiel peace treaty was signed on 14 January 1814, the Madras government was ordered in June 1815 to surrender Tranquebar, and 'The official transfer of sovereignty took place on 20 September', Gerhard Sievers Bille taking command.

1845: Tranquebar is sold to Britain: 'Tranquebar and most minor settlements sold' (no day on the page); the Tharangambadi page: 'Along with the Danish settlement of Serampore in Bengal, it was sold to the British in 1845.'

11 October 1845: Serampore is sold to Britain: 'On 11 October 1845, Serampore was sold to Britain.' The Danish India page also lists a sale of Serampore in 1839 without reconciling it with 1845; 1845 is used. The page adds that the other continental settlements were sold on 7 November 1845 (Balasore and the trading posts, which are not drawn).

16 October 1868: Denmark sells the Nicobars. Its presence 'ended formally on 16 October 1868 when it sold the rights to the Nicobar Islands to the United Kingdom' (no price on the page); Italy's attempt to buy them in 1864-1865 had failed.
1869: Danish India ends (infobox 'Established 1620 / disestablished 1869'): the Nicobars are formally annexed by Britain, which 'made them part of British India' (Nicobar Islands page).

wars.name: British occupation of Danish India, 1801-1802
wars.outcome: The British occupy Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore; the Danish flag is hoisted again at Tranquebar on 17 August 1802.
wars.note: The Tharangambadi page does not mention a 1801-1802 occupation.

wars.name: British occupation of Danish India, 1808-1815
wars.outcome: Occupied in the Napoleonic Wars (Tranquebar in February 1808); the Kiel peace treaty of 14 January 1814 restores them and sovereignty is transferred at Tranquebar on 20 September 1815.
wars.note: The war is the Napoleonic Wars (Tharangambadi page); no pages on it were opened.

certainty.note: The pages give no bounds for Tranquebar (one village and a fort) or Serampore (three named villages), so both are drawn as small circles; the Nicobar coasts are natural limits.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-c from 4 pages (of a budget of 5). Cliopatria's Danish India row covers only 1757-1808 (4 shapes, 2,222 km2 at most); the page's infobox gives 1620-1869, so this dossier starts at the Tranquebar treaty of 1620 and ends with the Nicobar annexation of 1869. Five new keyframes cover 1620-1756 and 1809-1869; the four Cliopatria shapes are all adjusted (Tranquebar missing until 1800, the Nicobars missing from 1800, the Serampore cell displaced about 25 km south).
Type 'colony', family 'nordic' as danish-gold-coast; the metropole (Denmark-Norway to 1814, the Kingdom of Denmark after) has no ledger event because no territory passed.
Page disagreements: Tranquebar treaty 19 November (Tharangambadi page; one Danish treaty collection) or 20 November 1620 (Danish India page; used); Serampore sold 1839 (Danish India page, unreconciled) or 11 October 1845 (both pages; used); the Danish India page says Danish settlers reached the 'Andaman Islands' in December 1755, which the plan covered with the Nicobars and is not used; the Tharangambadi page has Tranquebar occupied in February 1808 and does not mention 1801-1802.
Not drawn (trading posts, no territory on the page): Masulipatnam (by 1625), Pipli (by 1625 or 1626), Balasore (about 1636, reopened 1763 after a Maratha farman), Eddowa and Oddeway Torre (1695/96-1721/22 and 1696), Dannemarksnagore at Gondalpara, leased in 1698 for 30,000 rupees, Calicut (1752-1791). Balasore was occupied with Dansborg in 1801-1802 and 1808-1815 and sold on 7 November 1845 with the other continental settlements.
The occupation events are recorded here with british-empire as the occupier (the French India dossier does the same); the british-empire dossier does not mirror them because it opened none of the Danish pages.
Gazetteer names absent: Tranquebar (Tharangambadi, 79.85 E 11.03 N, drawn by coordinates), Serampore (Srirampur, 88.34 E 22.75 N), the Nicobar Islands as a group (a 190 km circle at 93.3 E 8.0 N stands in; the admin-1 'Andaman and Nicobar' includes the Andamans). Counterparts nayaks-of-thanjavur, nawabs-of-bengal, british-empire and british-raj exist or will exist.
